languageModelTools.name: netezza_get_context
languageModelTools.userDescription: Collect the current SQL, connection, referenced table DDL, and parser/linter diagnostics
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Collects a single context bundle for the active SQL editor or supplied SQL: active dialect, connection name, SQL text/selection, DDL for referenced tables, and current parser/linter diagnostics. Use this first when the user asks about "this query", "the current SQL", or a diagnostic. It replaces the former get_sql_schema and get_sql_diagnostics tools and requires no connection for parser diagnostics.

sql.description: Optional SQL text. When omitted, the active editor content or selection is used.

includeSchema.description: Include DDL for tables referenced by the SQL (default true).

languageModelTools.name: netezza_search_catalog
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search databases, schemas, tables, views, procedures, external tables, columns, or table locations
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Unified catalog discovery for the connected Netezza database. Choose objectType to list databases, schemas, tables, views, procedures, external tables, search columns or all objects by name pattern, or locate a table across databases. This replaces the former get_databases/get_schemas/get_tables/get_views/get_procedures/get_external_tables/search_schema/find_table_locations tools. Requires an active connection.

objectType.description: What to search. Defaults to tables.

pattern.description: Name pattern or table name. Required for columns, all, and locations.

database.description: Optional database scope. Defaults to the active connection database.

schema.description: Optional schema filter for tables, views, procedures, and external tables.

languageModelTools.name: netezza_get_object_details
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get DDL, columns, comments, statistics, dependencies, or workspace favorites for an object
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns structured metadata for one Netezza object. Select sections to control payload: ddl (CREATE statement), columns (names/types/nullability/keys), comments (table and column descriptions), stats (row count/skew/distribution), dependencies (foreign keys and view/procedure references), and favorites (workspace-curated table profiles and snippets). This replaces the former get_columns/get_ddl/get_comments/get_table_stats/get_dependencies/get_favorites tools.

objectName.description: Object name. Supports TABLE, SCHEMA.TABLE, DATABASE..TABLE, and DATABASE.SCHEMA.TABLE.

objectType.description: Object type used for DDL and dependency lookup. Defaults to table.

sections.description: Requested metadata sections. Defaults to ddl and columns.

languageModelTools.name: netezza_explain_sql
languageModelTools.userDescription: Run a read-only EXPLAIN and return plan structure, hotspots, risk, and raw plan
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs a read-only EXPLAIN for exactly one SELECT or WITH ... SELECT statement and returns structured plan nodes, edges, hotspots, overall risk, and the raw plan. Use it to diagnose performance. Tuning recommendations are intentionally left to the assistant and the JustyBase performance skill, which combine this output with object statistics and dependencies.

sql.description: SQL query to explain. Must be a single SELECT or WITH ... SELECT statement.

database.description: Optional database name to use. If not specified, uses the current database.

languageModelTools.name: netezza_validate_sql
languageModelTools.userDescription: Validates SQL with parser/linter rules (no database execution)
languageModelTools.modelDescription: This tool validates SQL using the built-in parser and linter pipeline. It returns syntax and semantic diagnostics with issue codes (e.g., SQLxxx, NZxxx, NZPxxx). Use this when you need offline validation without executing SQL. No database connection required.

sql.description: SQL code to validate. If not provided, uses the content of the currently active editor.

languageModelTools.name: netezza_validate_sql_on_database
languageModelTools.userDescription: Validates SQL against connected database using EXPLAIN
languageModelTools.modelDescription: This tool validates SQL on the connected IBM Netezza database by running EXPLAIN (without executing DML/SELECT results). Use this when parser validation passes but runtime/database context still needs verification. Requires an active database connection.

sql.description: SQL code to validate on database. If not provided, uses the content of the currently active editor.

languageModelTools.name: netezza_repair_procedure
languageModelTools.userDescription: Compiles a Netezza stored procedure and optionally runs a user-confirmed typed test CALL
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this tool to compile and repair one complete CREATE PROCEDURE or CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE block from the active SQL editor. The tool returns database compilation diagnostics and permits at most three attempts. Set mode='compile_only' to repair from compilation errors. Set mode='compile_and_call' and provide typed callArguments to run a test CALL after compilation; a separate explicit user confirmation is always required because CALL may modify database data. Pass the corrected complete procedure SQL in sql on subsequent attempts.

mode.description: Repair mode. compile_only uses compilation diagnostics; compile_and_call also tests the procedure with typed callArguments.

sql.description: Optional complete corrected CREATE PROCEDURE or CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE block. If omitted, uses the selected or current procedure block in the active editor.

callArguments.description: Typed values for CALL in declaration order. Required for compile_and_call; use [] for a no-argument procedure.

value.description: Value matching the declared type. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD.

languageModelTools.name: netezza_inspect_import_file
languageModelTools.userDescription: Inspects a source file and returns detected delimiter, inferred column types, and sample rows
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this tool before import to inspect CSV/TXT/XLSX/XLSB files. It infers delimiter and decimal separator, returns source-to-target column mapping preview, and shows sample rows. This tool does not write to database.

filePath.description: Path to source file to inspect.

sampleRows.description: Number of sample rows to return (default 5, max 20).

languageModelTools.name: netezza_propose_import_mapping
languageModelTools.userDescription: Proposes inferred source-to-target column mapping and CREATE TABLE SQL for import
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use this tool after file inspection to produce a proposed mapping for import. It infers target column names/types and returns proposed CREATE TABLE AS EXTERNAL SQL for the selected target table.

targetTable.description: Target table name in Netezza (for example MYDB.ADMIN.MYTABLE).

languageModelTools.name: netezza_get_dialect_reference
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get Netezza SQL, optimization, or NZPLSQL reference guidance
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the JustyBase reference rules for the active dialect: SQL naming conventions and optimization guidance, NZPLSQL procedure constraints, or both. Use it before rewriting or reviewing Netezza SQL when dialect-specific rules matter.

walkthroughs.title: JustyBase: First 5 Minutes
walkthroughs.description: Connect to a database, run your first query, and validate SQL.

steps.title: 1) Create connection
steps.description: Open the connection dialog and add your host, user and password.

steps.title: 2) Run your first query
steps.description: Run current statement with Ctrl+Enter / F5 and open the result panel.

steps.title: 3) Validate SQL quality
steps.description: Use on-demand linting and parser validation to catch mistakes early.

justybase.ui.mode.description: Presentation mode for host-owned VS Code UI surfaces. Shared UI is available for supported panels.

justybase.highlightActiveStatement.description: Enable highlighting of the active SQL statement.

justybase.longQueryAlertThreshold.description: Notify when a query execution exceeds this threshold (in minutes). Set to 0 to disable.

justybase.pythonPath.description: Python executable for running scripts. Use justybase.pythonArgs for interpreter arguments.

justybase.pythonArgs.description: Arguments passed to the configured Python executable before the script, for example ["-3"] with the Windows py launcher.

justybase.showConflictWarnings.description: Show warning when other SQL extensions (SQLTools, MS SQL, etc.) are detected that may cause conflicts.

justybase.formatSQL.tabWidth.description: Number of spaces for indentation in formatted SQL.

justybase.linter.enabled.description: Enable SQL linting for Netezza files.

justybase.linter.mode.description: Linting mode. Advanced parser-based SQL validation is always used.

justybase.sql.showHoverTooltips.description: Show SQL editor hover tooltips for aliases, tables, and columns.

justybase.sql.showSelectionActionHover.description: Show Run/Export action links when hovering over a non-object part of selected SQL.

justybase.sql.showSelectionExecutionCode.description: Show Run/Export actions in the lightbulb menu (Quick Actions) for selected SQL.

justybase.sql.showInlineTypeHints.description: Show inline SQL type hints for resolved qualified columns (for example: alias.column INT8).

justybase.sql.joinNameHeuristics.description: Allow lower-priority JOIN suggestions based on matching cached key and column names when no declared or configured relationship is available.

justybase.sql.joinKnowledgeIndex.description: Learn from workspace .sql files: lower-priority JOIN suggestions and FROM-object usage bands. Off by default; manual decisions and catalog metadata are unaffected. Only identifiers, counters and timestamps are stored; no SQL text, literals or result values. Learning from executed queries is controlled by justybase.sql.learnFromExecutedQueries.

justybase.sql.learnFromExecutedQueries.description: Learn from successful Netezza queries you run (and, once, from the query history): JOINs, FROM sources and columns you use repeatedly rank higher. Stored locally as identifiers, counters and timestamps only; no SQL text, literals or result values. Existing knowledge is kept when turned off; clear it in the JOIN knowledge manager.

justybase.sql.joinKnowledgeIndexGitWindo.description: Git history window used only to select which workspace .sql files are indexed. 0 means all files. Dirty, untracked and open files are always included; Git history itself is never parsed as evidence.

justybase.sql.autoJoinAliases.description: Generate a unique table alias when accepting a JOIN completion.

enumDescriptions: Insert completed keywords in upper case (SELECT).
Insert completed keywords in lower case (select).
Follow the typed prefix: lower case when the typed letters are lower case, otherwise upper case.
justybase.sql.completionKeywordCase.description: Case of SQL keywords inserted by completion. The suggestion list itself always shows keywords in upper case.

enumDescriptions: One column per line with leading commas (`    , D.COL`).
One column per line with trailing commas (`    D.COL,`).
All columns on the original line, separated by `, `.
justybase.sql.expandStarLayout.description: Layout of the column list produced by the "Expand * to column list" refactoring and the NZ001 quick fix. Unaliased tables receive a generated alias; existing aliases are reused.

justybase.sql.joinAliases.description: Workspace table-to-alias overrides used by JOIN completions.

justybase.sql.joinRelations.description: Workspace virtual JOIN relationships. Table identities use database/schema/table fields and columns map left to right.

justybase.sql.personalizeFromObjects.description: Apply manual SQL-object preferences (pin, boost, demote, exclude) to FROM source completion. JOIN ranking and the two documented Stage 1 behavior changes are unaffected when this is disabled.

justybase.sql.groupByGhostText.markdownDescription: After `GROUP BY ` show the non-aggregated SELECT expressions as inline ghost text; press `Tab` to accept. Shown only when the SELECT at that level has an aggregate.

enumDescriptions: After JOIN show a target you confirmed, configured or starred; after JOIN <table> show its ON condition when exactly one is likely.
As afterJoin, and on an empty line that ends the FROM clause of a SELECT also offer the whole JOIN.
justybase.sql.joinGhostText.markdownDescription: Show a confident JOIN suggestion as inline ghost text; press `Tab` to accept. Targets are offered only for relations you configured, confirmed or starred (executed JOINs rank first but are not guessed as the next JOIN); ON conditions also come from catalog keys and executed queries. Nothing is shown when two suggestions are equally likely.

justybase.sql.personalizeColumns.description: Order column completions by how broadly each column is used in workspace SQL files and successful executions (requires the JOIN Knowledge index). Only column order changes; no column is added or hidden.

justybase.linter.rules.description: Configure SQL linter rules severity. Available rules: NZ001 (SELECT *), NZ002 (DELETE without WHERE), NZ003 (UPDATE without WHERE), NZ004 (CROSS JOIN), NZ005 (Leading wildcard LIKE), NZ006 (ORDER BY without LIMIT), NZ007 (Inconsistent keyword case), NZ008 (TRUNCATE), NZ009 (Multiple OR), NZ010 (Missing table alias), NZ011 (CTAS missing DISTRIBUTE ON), NZ012 (UPDATE with AS alias), NZ013 (UNION vs UNION ALL), NZ014 (OR in JOIN condition), NZ015 (Function in WHERE), NZ016 (Implicit Casting in Join), NZ017 (Double Quoted Identifiers), NZ018 (Self-referential JOIN), NZ019 (CASE without END), NZ020 (IN (SELECT) subquery), NZ023 (Qualify table references), NZP001 (Missing BEGIN_PROC/END_PROC), NZP002 (Missing LANGUAGE clause), NZP003 (Missing RETURNS clause), NZP004 (Unmatched BEGIN/END blocks), NZP005 (Unmatched IF statement), NZP006 (Unmatched LOOP statement), NZP008 (Unused variable), NZP010 (RAISE without severity), NZP011 (Missing INTO in SELECT), NZP012 (Incorrect ELSIF syntax), NZP013 (Missing THEN), NZP017 (Unmatched CASE), NZP022 (OUT/INOUT assignment), NZP024 (Missing RETURN). On-demand procedure heuristics: NZP007, NZP009, NZP014, NZP015, NZP016, NZP018, NZP019, NZP020, NZP025, NZP026, NZP027, NZP028, NZP029, NZP030. Values: error, warning, information, hint, off.

justybase.enableStreaming.description: Enable streaming mode for query results. When enabled, results are sent to the UI in chunks for better memory efficiency and faster first-data display with large result sets.

justybase.streamingChunkSize.description: Number of rows per chunk when streaming mode is enabled. Larger chunks are more efficient but use more memory.

justybase.schemaSearch.searchAllDatabase.description: When enabled, Schema Search queries all databases on the connection. When disabled, only the active/default database is searched (recommended for large Netezza warehouses).

justybase.cacheTTL.description: Metadata cache time-to-live in hours. Cached schema, tables, and columns will be refreshed after this period. Default: 12 hours.

justybase.metadataCache.diskPersistence.description: Persist metadata cache to disk between VS Code sessions (enabled by default). When enabled, metadata is loaded instantly from disk on startup, avoiding slow database prefetches. Disable only if the cache file takes up too much disk space.

justybase.metadataCache.crossWindowSync.description: Synchronize metadata cache across multiple VS Code windows using file-system watch + polling. When enabled, a window that finishes a prefetch notifies other windows to reload from disk instead of re-fetching from the database.

justybase.metadataCache.memoryWarningByt.description: Estimated in-memory metadata cache size (bytes) above which a warning is logged when viewing cache stats. Default: 256 MB.

justybase.query.maxParallelPerTab.description: Maximum independent SQL executions per editor tab when Keep Connection Open is disabled.

justybase.query.maxParallelGlobal.description: Maximum independent SQL executions across editor tabs in this extension host.

justybase.query.rowLimit.description: Maximum number of rows to fetch per query execution

justybase.query.executionTimeout.description: Query execution timeout in seconds (default: 1 hour)

justybase.metadata.sessionSweep.enabled.description: Automatically drop stale metadata catalog sessions that exceed the configured age (DROP SESSION). Only affects sessions created by metadata/prefetch queries; user queries are never touched.

justybase.metadata.sessionSweep.interval.description: How often the metadata session sweeper checks for stale sessions.

justybase.metadata.sessionSweep.maxAgeMi.description: Metadata catalog sessions older than this many minutes are dropped automatically (DROP SESSION). Requires system admin privileges on Netezza.

justybase.metadata.queryConcurrency.description: Maximum number of concurrent metadata catalog queries outside the dedicated full-refresh column pool. The safe default is one query per connection; increase only when the Netezza workload allows it. Applied to per-connection query limiting in the extension host and metadata warm-up batching in the language server. Default: 1.

justybase.metadata.fullRefreshColumnConn.description: Physical Netezza sessions used by the column stage of a full metadata refresh (1–8). One is safest; higher values can shorten refreshes by processing independent databases in parallel. Additional sessions are optional and fall back to the primary session if they cannot be opened.

justybase.metadata.popularDatabases.description: Number of recently used Netezza databases warmed together with the active database. The rest stay lazy and are loaded when opened. Default: 2. Set to 0 to warm only the active database.

enumDescriptions: Authoring reads the shadow cache only; a missing scope shows a refresh placeholder.
Authoring reads the cache and may query the live catalog when the user explicitly expands or requests data (DataGrip-like).
Preserve the legacy behaviour: fall back to a live catalog query whenever the cache misses.
justybase.metadata.liveFallback.description: Controls whether metadata consumers may fall back to a live Netezza catalog query on a cache miss. Completion and validation always prefer the shadow cache.

justybase.sqlParser.fastPathThreshold.description: Character count threshold for using fast lexer-based SQL statement splitting. Files larger than this use the legacy character-scan method which is faster for huge files. Default: ~1.5M characters (1572864).

justybase.safeExecute.enabled.description: Show confirmation dialog before executing risky SQL (DELETE/UPDATE without WHERE, TRUNCATE).

justybase.codeLens.enabled.description: Show CodeLens toolbar at top of document and per-statement actions (Run, Explain, Visualize Query Flow, Export).

justybase.codeLens.run.description: Show 'Run' button in top-level CodeLens toolbar.

justybase.codeLens.runBatch.description: Show 'Run Batch' button in top-level CodeLens toolbar.

justybase.codeLens.openAsXlsx.description: Show 'Open as XLSX' button in top-level CodeLens toolbar.

justybase.codeLens.openAsXlsb.description: Show 'Open as XLSB' button in top-level CodeLens toolbar.

justybase.codeLens.export.description: Show 'Export' button in top-level CodeLens toolbar.

justybase.codeLens.markdown.description: Show 'MD' (Markdown export) button in top-level CodeLens toolbar.

justybase.codeLens.explain.description: Show 'Explain' button in top-level CodeLens toolbar.

justybase.codeLens.import.description: Show 'Import' button in top-level CodeLens toolbar.

justybase.ddl.maxTablesForContext.description: Maximum number of tables to include in Copilot DDL context

justybase.ddl.cacheTTL.description: DDL cache time-to-live in milliseconds (default: 1 hour)

justybase.copilot.maxWorkspaceProfilesIn.description: Maximum number of workspace Copilot table profiles included in one Copilot request context.

justybase.copilot.enabled.description: Register JustyBase AI tools and enable AI-assisted SQL workflows. When disabled, the extension does not register its language-model tools; the read-only MCP server is controlled separately.

justybase.mcp.enabled.description: Register the read-only Netezza MCP server (stdio) for Copilot Chat in VS Code. Passwords are passed to the server process via environment variables and are never written to disk.

justybase.mcp.connectionName.description: Name of the Netezza connection explicitly selected for both MCP transports. The active editor connection is not used. Select it in JustyBase Settings → MCP Server.

justybase.mcp.externalEnabled.description: Start the Netezza MCP server in HTTP mode on 127.0.0.1 so other MCP clients on this machine (Cursor, Claude Desktop, ...) can use the read-only schema tools. Runs only while VS Code is open.

justybase.mcp.port.description: TCP port for the Netezza MCP server HTTP mode (127.0.0.1 only).

justybase.logging.level.description: Logging level for extension output channel

justybase.results.maxDataResults.description: Maximum number of data result sets to keep per SQL file. Older unpinned results are automatically pruned when this limit is exceeded.

justybase.results.maxPinnedDataResults.description: Maximum number of result sets that can be manually pinned per SQL file.

justybase.results.diskBackedResults.enab.description: Spill large result sets to a temporary SQLite database to reduce memory usage.

justybase.results.diskBackedResults.rowT.description: Hard upper row count before disk-backed storage must activate (when enabled).

justybase.results.diskBackedResults.memo.description: Spill result rows to SQLite once this row count is reached (host RAM).
Approximate host-memory budget in bytes before results spill to SQLite.

justybase.results.diskBackedResults.inse.description: Rows per SQLite INSERT batch during spill.

justybase.results.diskBackedResults.idle.description: Spill idle in-memory results to SQLite after this many minutes without interaction (0 = disabled).
Minimum row count for idle spill eligibility.

justybase.results.diskBackedResults.disk.description: Total on-disk budget in MB shared by all disk-backed result stores. When a spill would cross it, the result stays in memory and a warning is shown.

justybase.results.gridFontFamily.description: Font family used by the main results data grid. Use 'editor' to follow the current VS Code editor font, or provide a custom CSS font-family stack. Available: JetBrains Mono, Fira Code, Cascadia Code, Source Code Pro, IBM Plex Mono, Menlo, Consolas, Ubuntu Mono, Droid Sans Mono, Courier New.

justybase.results.gridFontSize.description: Font size (px) used by the main results data grid and row view.

justybase.results.integerGrouping.description: Use grouped thousands for integer-like result columns such as SMALLINT, INT, and BIGINT.

justybase.results.decimalGrouping.description: Use grouped thousands for NUMERIC and DECIMAL result columns.

justybase.results.groupSeparator.description: Grouping separator used in formatted result grid numbers. The default is a space.

justybase.results.decimalSeparator.description: Decimal separator used in formatted NUMERIC and DECIMAL result values.

justybase.results.decimalScale.description: Default number of decimal places shown for NUMERIC and DECIMAL result columns.

justybase.results.preserveTrailingZeros.description: Preserve trailing zeros when rendering NUMERIC and DECIMAL result values.

justybase.results.roundingMode.description: Rounding mode used when formatted result values need to reduce decimal precision.

justybase.results.useFormattedValuesForE.description: Use formatted display values instead of raw values for result exports initiated from the results grid.

justybase.results.copyFormat.markdownDescription: Default plain text format for Ctrl+C in the results grid. `tabbed` uses tab-separated columns (plain text). `markdown` uses Markdown table syntax. `csv` uses comma-separated values. `csv-semicolon` uses semicolon-separated values (useful when comma is a decimal separator).

enumDescriptions: Excel binary workbook (.xlsb) - smaller and faster, opens in Microsoft Excel
Excel workbook (.xlsx) - wider compatibility (LibreOffice, Google Sheets)
justybase.results.defaultExcelFormat.markdownDescription: Default Excel format preselected in the SQL Results **Export** menu and used by **Export & Open** and the quick Excel actions. `xlsb` is smaller and faster but opens only in Microsoft Excel; `xlsx` is more widely compatible.

justybase.filePreview.maxRows.description: Maximum number of rows for Parquet and result-grid previews. The Excel/CSV spreadsheet view streams all rows and ignores this limit.

justybase.filePreview.maxColumns.description: Maximum number of columns to read for the spreadsheet preview (XLSX, XLSB, CSV). Wider sheets keep their remaining columns available through export or Add to Data Workspace.

justybase.filePreview.csvPreviewMode.description: Choose the default preview mode for CSV files. 'custom' uses the Netezza Data File Preview with advanced features. 'native' uses VS Code's built-in CSV preview.

justybase.importWizard.defaultMode.description: Default mode for the Import Data command. Use prompt to choose each time, simple to keep the current best-effort flow, or advanced to open the import wizard directly.

justybase.importWizard.previewRowCount.description: Number of rows shown in the advanced import wizard preview grid.

justybase.importWizard.validationSampleS.description: Number of preview rows validated synchronously in the advanced import wizard.

justybase.importWizard.backgroundValidat.description: Enable asynchronous background validation for large imports. When enabled, validation runs in the background after the initial preview loads.
Number of rows to validate in the background. Higher values provide more thorough validation but take longer. Default: 20000.
